what: Rexford Industrial owns warehouses in Southern California only: about 50 million square feet of infill industrial property in Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego and the Inland Empire.
customers: Distributors, manufacturers and logistics operators needing space close to the ports and the population.
moat: Southern California industrial land is effectively unbuildable: the region has the busiest ports in America, enormous demand and almost no sites left, which has driven rents up for a decade.
risks: A $473M reported loss after property write-downs as Southern California rents fell
Market rents in the Inland Empire have dropped sharply from their peak
opportunities: $262M of free cash flow and a 21.1% operating margin
Revenue grew from $452M to $1.0B in four years
Even after the fall, rents on leases signed years ago are far below market, so renewals still reset upward
watch: Market rent trends in the Inland Empire and the spread on lease renewals.
